records.reference: OpenStax, College Physics 2e, Chapter 9 "Statics and Torque" (torque, the second condition for equilibrium, levers).
records.old: (a) A moment is the turning effect of a force, found by M = F × d, where d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force. In the jembe, the blade-soil contact is the pivot. Where the farmer grips decides d. A longer handle, or gripping further from the blade, increases d, so the same effort produces a larger moment. That is why Amina, with the 90 cm handle, broke the soil more easily than Juma with the 30 cm handle, although the blade and the effort were the same. Engineers and farmers therefore design tools with long handles or wide grips to increase the turning effect without increasing the effort needed.
records.new: (a) Claim: Where the farmer grips decides how big the turning effect is, so a longer handle lets the same push turn the blade more easily. Evidence: with the same effort F, a 90 cm handle gives a distance d three times bigger than a 30 cm handle (0.9 m against 0.3 m), so the moment is three times bigger (for example 80 N × 0.9 m = 72 N·m against 80 N × 0.3 m = 24 N·m); in our metre-rule data the rule balanced only when F × d was equal on both sides. Reasoning: a moment is the turning effect of a force, M = F × d, where d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot (the blade-soil contact) to the line of action of the force. For the same F, a larger d gives a larger moment, so Amina, with the 90 cm handle, broke the soil more easily than Juma with the 30 cm handle, although the blade and the effort were the same. Engineers and farmers therefore design tools with long handles to increase the turning effect without increasing the effort needed.
